I've completed all four research tracks. Here's your career brief.

# Career Brief: Breaking into LA Post-Production IT/Engineering

## 1. What employers expect + 3 recurring requirements
I read three real LA postings (Promise Studios, Paramount ×2). Across them, the same three requirement clusters recur:

1. **Core IT systems administration** — Windows + Linux administration, Active Directory / identity & access management, MDM (Jamf/Intune), and networking basics (VLANs, DHCP, IP, firewalls).
2. **Media-specific tooling** — the Avid ecosystem (Media Composer, Interplay, MediaCentral; **ACSR certification explicitly "preferred"** at Paramount), plus enterprise file transfer (Aspera/Signiant) and storage (NAS, cloud, archive/MAM).
3. **Cloud + scripting** — at least one cloud platform (AWS/Azure/OCI/GCP) with VM/storage troubleshooting, and scripting/automation (Bash, PowerShell, or Python).

**Two training/certification routes that map directly onto those gaps:**
- **Avid certification path** (avid.com/learning/certification) — Avid's post-production credentials, including the ACSR support certification named in Paramount's posting, and the newer Avid/Post Super micro-certifications ("Post-Production Workflow for High-End TV & Film" and "Post-Production Delivery for HETV & Film").
- **Key Code Education's Post Production Engineer program** (keycodeeducation.com) — a hands-on program covering post-production workflows, system configuration, and media engineering across Avid, DaVinci Resolve, and Adobe, explicitly aimed at people who "support and manage professional media production environments."

**Realistic verdict:** Yes, this is trainable into — but the entry door is a *general IT* role, not a "post-production engineer" title. Promise Studios' junior posting accepts "1 to 3 years in IT support, or equivalent hands-on depth," lists studio/post experience only as *preferred*, and states a "real growth path into infrastructure engineering." The media-specific layer (Avid, Aspera, codecs) is the bridgeable gap the two training routes above close. Expect ~$120–135K at the junior step, $136K+ at the mid-level technician step.

## 2. IATSE Local 700 (Motion Picture Editors Guild) — West Coast entry path
From the official **Join West Coast** page (left open for you):

- **Get a union job first.** The Guild tells you to first secure union employment; you must then join Local 700 **within 30 days of your date of hire**.
- **Roster before you can work:** Most classifications working in LA County must be on the **CSATF Industry Experience Roster** *prior* to accepting union employment (required for all classifications except Foley Artist and Sound Service Person Y16). **"Engineer" is one of the Local 700 classifications** in their dropdown — so the IT/engineering side of post does have a union path.
- **Roster ≠ membership.** The page stresses these are separate processes; roster placement doesn't auto-trigger membership or vice versa.
- **Qualifying experience:** Work must match work covered by the Local 700 Agreements or Videotape Supplemental Agreement, performed in the US and/or Puerto Rico. Industrial/educational films do **not** count; SVOD eligibility varies (verify with a Roster Specialist).
- **Proof required:** A letter from your non-union employer (company letterhead; from the payroll company if you're payroll-paid) **plus** proof of payment (W-2s, 1099s, paystubs, or cancelled checks) at no less than California minimum wage.
- **Days required:** Vary by classification (the page has a per-classification dropdown; the exact Engineer day count is JS-rendered and I couldn't extract it — the CSATF portal shows the specific number once you start an application).
- **Fees:** Roster placement is **free** (all online via thehub.org). You must complete Safety Courses **A (General Production Safety), HP1, and WVP** (sound classifications add Course K). Membership itself has a **one-time initiation & processing fee** (varies by contract; payment plan available — half down, half within 6 months; the fee schedule link didn't resolve to a readable page, so confirm current amounts with Membership).
- **Orientation:** New Member Orientation via Zoom (roster process, membership duties, pension/health plans).
- **Contacts on the page:** Membership — Tracy Pacio (323) 978-1087, Tylene Joye (323) 978-1085, membership@editorsguild.com; CSATF — 2710 Winona Ave, Burbank, (818) 565-0550.

**Practical sequence:** non-union IT work in post → accumulate qualifying days → CSATF roster → union hire → join Local 700 within 30 days.

## 3. Live job examples (all open in tabs)
1. **IT Support Engineer (Junior) — Promise Studios — Los Angeles (on-site), $120K–$135K + bonus.** The clearest entry point: 1–3 yrs IT support, macOS/Windows admin, cloud VM troubleshooting, studio transfer/review tools (LucidLink, Aspera, Box, Flow Capture); MDM, post-production exposure, networking, and scripting are *preferred*; states a growth path into infrastructure engineering. **Visa/work authorization: no mention** in the posting (EEO statement only).
2. **Media Maintenance Technician (403g) — Paramount — Los Angeles (Studio City), $136,281/yr** (updated Aug 24, 2026). The mid-level benchmark: 5 yrs end-to-end media workflows (ingest, transcoding, QC, delivery), hands-on Avid (Media Composer/Interplay/MediaCentral, ACSR preferred) + Pro Tools, Windows/Linux, Active Directory, AWS/Azure/OCI, Aspera/Signiant, JAMF, scripting. **Visa/work authorization: no mention.**
3. **Senior Manager, Media Operations — Paramount — Los Angeles (Hollywood), $98K–$125K** (posted Sep 2, 2026). The senior/lead version: storage & archive strategy, AD security groups, Avid/Premiere/Resolve, cloud (AWS/Azure/OCI), Signiant/Aspera, MAM/DAM, plus team management. **Visa/work authorization: no mention.**

(Context: Company 3's "Systems Engineer, Sr – Post Production Avid Engineer," Hollywood, $85K–$120K, is a good spec reference but that posting is **expired** — closed 07/17/2026.)

## 4. Rosie O'Donnell–Trump feud — short dated timeline
- **Dec 19–20, 2006** — After Trump gives Miss USA Tara Conner a "second chance," O'Donnell savages him on *The View* ("snake-oil salesman… Donald, sit and spin"); Trump calls her "a real loser" and "a woman out of control" to People. *(CNN)*
- **Dec 14, 2011** — Trump tweets he "feels sorry" for O'Donnell's fiancée's parents after her engagement to Michelle Rounds; she replies "wow u r an ass." *(CNN)*
- **Aug 21, 2012** — After O'Donnell's heart attack, Trump tweets "Rosie, get better fast. I'm starting to miss you!"; she replies "r u trying to kill me?" *(CNN)*
- **Aug 6, 2015** — At the first GOP primary debate, asked about "pigs, slobs and dogs," Trump: "Only Rosie O'Donnell." *(CNN)*
- **Sep 26, 2016** — At the first presidential debate, Trump revives the feud against Clinton's sexism charge: "Somebody who has been very vicious to me, Rosie O'Donnell." *(CNN)*
- **May 11, 2017** — Trump tweets "We finally agree on something Rosie" over the Comey firing; O'Donnell: "u r a sadistic man." *(CNN)*
- **Mar 2025** — On RTÉ's *Late Late Show*, O'Donnell credits her move to Ireland to Trump's second inauguration (Jan 2025); Trump has threatened to revoke her US citizenship. *(People, Jul 22, 2026)*

## Pages left open for you
- **Tab 1 — editorsguild.com/Join/Join-West-Coast** ← the most useful union page (exact wording of steps, roster, fees, contacts)
- **Tab 2 — Promise Studios "IT Support Engineer (Junior)"** (Ashby)
- **Tab 3 — Paramount "Media Maintenance Technician"** (EntertainmentCareers)
- **Tab 9 — Paramount "Senior Manager, Media Operations"** (EntertainmentCareers)
- **Tab 4 — CNN feud timeline** and **Tab 6 — People's 20-year feud explainer**

Hey, I’m trying to figure out whether I could realistically break into post-production in LA, especially on the IT/engineering side of media and entertainment rather than editing itself. I want a realistic sense of the entry path before I get too attached to the idea.

Can you help me look it up? I’d start with what employers in media/entertainment usually expect from IT engineers, and then pull together a few recurring requirements I keep seeing—like three common ones—and two actual training or certification routes that could get me there. I want to know if this is something I could train into from where I’m at now.

After that, I also want to compare the union route. Can you check the Motion Picture Editors Guild site for the West Coast/LA path to joining IATSE Local 700? I’m looking for the actual steps, eligibility, anything about applications, rosters, fees, or required experience. If there are separate Local 700 pages that matter, open the important ones in their own tabs and leave the most useful one open so I can read the exact wording myself.

Then go back to Google and find current LA or broader West Coast jobs that actually match the skills and requirements you found earlier.
